record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: For a queueing system with a fixed threshold t, what scheduling policy minimizes the tail probability P{Response Time > t} rather than only its asymptotic behavior as t goes to infinity?

evidence.quote: while comparing the asymptotic tail under different scheduling policies is interesting from a theoretical standpoint, it does not solve the practical question of scheduling to minimize P {Response Time > t} for a particular t; this remains an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server preemptive queueing system in which jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$ and have i.i.d.\ service requirements drawn from a known distribution $S$ with finite mean, where the system is in steady state with load $ho = \lambda \mathbb{E}[S] < 1$. A scheduling policy $\pi$ is a (possibly size-aware, possibly age-based) rule that, at every instant, selects which job in the system to serve, and the response time $T_\pi$ of a job under policy $\pi$ is the time from its arrival until its completion. Fix a finite threshold $t > 0$.

Determine the scheduling policy $\pi^\star$ that minimizes the steady-state tail probability
$$\mathbb{P}\{T_\pi > t\}$$
over all work-conserving (or possibly more general) scheduling policies, as opposed to merely minimizing the asymptotic decay rate $\lim_{t	o\infty}  rac{1}{t}\log \mathbb{P}\{T_\pi > t\}$. Characterize $\pi^\star$ either in closed form or via a structural description, and identify how $\pi^\star$ depends on $t$, on the service distribution $S$, and on the load $ho$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and theses on multiserver and single-server scheduling state that essentially nothing is known about scheduling to optimize the tail of response time at a fixed finite threshold, although first results on optimizing asymptotic tail metrics have appeared. No source identifies a policy that minimizes P{Response Time > t} for arbitrary finite t, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Scheduling in Multiserver Queues (Grosof thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: while it is known that SRPT scheduling optimizes mean response time, essentially nothing is known about scheduling to optimize the tail of response time
status_evidence.claim: Optimizing the tail of response time at finite thresholds remains largely unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Finite-Time Information-Theoretic Bounds in Queueing Control
status_evidence.snippet: first finite-time information-theoretic lower bounds and new policies that achieve them ... little is known about ... worst-case performance and fundamental limitations in non-asymptotic settings
status_evidence.claim: Finite-time (non-asymptotic) tail/queue-length optimization in queueing scheduling is an active and largely open area.
